pull.title: wallet: harden the read-only BDB parser against crafted files
pull.body:
The read-only BDB parser in migrate.cpp runs on any file passed to `migratewallet`
(RPC or GUI) or `bitcoin-wallet`. #34959 added checks for btree levels and overflow
lengths, which stop simple cycles, but a crafted file can still make the parser hang
or use a lot of memory:

- A btree page can be the child of more than one internal page. Its level still
  checks out, so it gets parsed again for every path that reaches it. On master an
  ~8 KB file built this way doesn't finish.
- An overflow page with no data doesn't count toward the length #34959 checks, so
  two such pages pointing at each other loop forever. Separately, any number of
  records can point at the same overflow chain, and each one reads and stores its
  own copy.
- All of a page's index entries can point at the same record, which then gets read
  and kept once per entry. A single 64 KB page can turn into ~500 MB this way. On
  master a 256 KB file took `migratewallet` from 54 MB to ~800 MB.

The first two are fixed by tracking visited pages (the approach from #34946): btree
pages in one set, and overflow pages in another that covers the whole tree. For the
third, a page is rejected once its records add up to more than the page size.

This shouldn't affect real wallets. In a valid btree every page has a single parent
and every overflow page belongs to a single record. Records on a page can't overlap
either, since the parser already rejects databases that allow duplicates.

Each fix comes with a test in db_tests.cpp that builds the bad file by hand, plus a
test that a page filled to the last byte still parses. `wallet_migration.py` passes
with v28.2.

The last commit adds two errors from #34959 to the `wallet_bdb_parser` fuzz target.
They were missing, so the target aborted on inputs that reach them. I ran into this
while feeding mutated copies of the test files through the target.

Supersedes #35992.

events.message:
wallet, bdbro: Reject revisited btree pages

Validating btree page levels stops a page from being its own ancestor,
but a page can still be reachable from more than one parent while
keeping a consistent level. Such a page, and everything below it, is
parsed again for every path that reaches it, so a small file can
describe an exponential amount of work. A valid btree references each
page once, so keep track of the pages already visited and reject any
that is seen again.

wallet, bdbro: Reject revisited overflow pages

Enforcing overflow data lengths stops a chain whose pages carry data,
but overflow pages that carry no data never advance the accumulated
length, so a chain that cycles through empty overflow pages loops
forever. Any number of records can also point at the same chain, which
is then read and stored once per record.

In a valid database each overflow page belongs to one record, so keep
track of the overflow pages visited across the whole tree and reject
one that is seen again.

wallet, bdbro: Enforce that a page's records fit in the page

A page's index entries each point at a record that is read and kept, but
the offsets are not checked against each other. A page whose entries all
point at the same record is therefore read into entries * len bytes of
memory, so a single page can be read into far more than its own size. In
a valid page the records do not overlap and cannot be larger than the
page, so track their total size while reading and reject a page whose
records do not fit.

fuzz: Add missing BDB overflow errors to wallet_bdb_parser

#34959 added two errors for invalid overflow records, but did not add
them to the errors the wallet_bdb_parser target expects, so the target
aborts on inputs that reach them.

wallet, bdbro: Reject oversized overflow page data

An overflow page stores the length of its data in hf_offset, which is
not checked against the page size. A 512 byte page can claim up to 65535
bytes, read from the pages that follow it, so a file can be read into up
to about 128 times its own size.

BDB never stores more on an overflow page than fits after the page
header, so reject a page whose data does not fit.

events.body:
Pushed a new check and fixed a test gap.

e0c98a22a6: reject overflow pages whose data length exceeds `page_size - 26`, the BDB per-page maximum.
8b0b1f026f: the internal-page test record is now deleted, so only the size check can reject it. Addresses @vicjuma's [comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35990#discussion_r4453775019).
The rest is test formatting only.

comments.body: Works as expected, and the unit test fails when commented out, meaning that, as per the test master is accepting record sizes exceeding the file size **Before:** **After:**

Thanks, the old test was rejected by the revisited page check first. Fixed in 8b0b1f026f: the record is now marked deleted, so only this check catches it.
